audits.title: 135 A Quality Improvement Project Aimed to Reduce the Number of Patients on Bournville Ward Suffering with Constipation
audits.standard: Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham guidelines: conservative measures (fluid, fibre, exercise) before laxatives
audits.setting: Bournville Ward, Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, geriatrics

cycle1.result: Constipation recognised in 57%; 64% of these developed it in hospital; 20% had complications.

audits.intervention: Teaching sessions for ward staff and weekly MDT discussion of constipated patients, with early non-laxative measures if bowels not opened for over 2 days.

cycle2.result: Patient education up 19%, cause recognition up 27%, non-laxative methods up 30%; inpatient-developed constipation down 6% and complications down 4%.

audits.other_findings: Only a small impact on constipation prevalence and complications.
audits.citation: Vasudev A, Mohamed I, Jacques H, Nicolson P. 135 A Quality Improvement Project Aimed to Reduce the Number of Patients on Bournville Ward Suffering with Constipation. Age and Ageing. 2021;50(Supplement_1):i12-i42. doi:10.1093/ageing/afab030.96.

audits.title: 56 Quality Improvement Project on the Bowel Charts in An Elderly Care Ward in Basildon University Hospital
audits.standard: Completion of bowel charts (no formal standard stated)
audits.setting: Elderly care ward, Basildon University Hospital

cycle1.result: About 23% of bowel charts complete in the initial audit.

audits.intervention: Interventions introduced in steps (details not stated), with three further audits over 5 months.

cycle2.result: Bowel chart completion rose to 60% (an improvement of 37%).

audits.other_findings: Four audits in total over 5 months; improvement sustained except at weekends because of staffing.
audits.citation: Hakim R, Ali M, Wijenyake I. 56 Quality Improvement Project on the Bowel Charts in An Elderly Care Ward in Basildon University Hospital. Age and Ageing. 2020;49(Supplement_1):i14-i17. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz186.10.

audits.title: P06 A quality improvement project to improve use of bowel charts in surgical wards
audits.setting: All adult surgical wards, district general hospital (King's Mill Hospital)

cycle1.result: Bowel chart present in 79% of nursing folders; bowel movements documented in 25% of nursing and 30% of medical notes.

audits.intervention: Bowel chart paper colour changed from white to yellow with identical content.

cycle2.result: Bowel chart present in 90%; documentation in nursing and medical notes 74% and 69%.

audits.other_findings: The change was rolled out trust-wide.
audits.citation: Bharmal A. P06 A quality improvement project to improve use of bowel charts in surgical wards. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac231.006.

cycle1.result: Baseline audit (figures not given in abstract).

audits.title: Improving Constipation in Critical Care Patients: A Single-Centre Prospective Cohort Closed-Loop Clinical Audit.
audits.setting: Intensive Care Unit, Royal Liverpool University Hospital

cycle1.result: Senna and docusate prescribed on admission in 50% of medical and 25% of surgical patients; bowels opened within 48 hours in 64.3% of medical and 36.1% of surgical patients.

cycle2.result: Senna and docusate prescribed in 90% of medical and 13.2% of surgical patients; bowels opened within 48 hours in 90% of medical and 21.1% of surgical patients.

audits.other_findings: No statistically significant change between cycles; surgical patients' care was set by parent teams.
audits.citation: Xu N, Khoo CC. Improving Constipation in Critical Care Patients: A Single-Centre Prospective Cohort Closed-Loop Clinical Audit. Cureus. 2026;18(1):e101232. doi:10.7759/cureus.101232. PMID: 41669582.

audits.title: Improving the Assessment and Management of Constipation in Elderly Inpatients: A Quality Improvement Project in a Geriatric Ward.
audits.standard: National guidelines for managing constipation in frail patients
audits.setting: Frailty ward, Fairfield General Hospital, Bury

cycle1.result: Abdominal exam documented 33% (n=5); constipating medication review 26% (n=4); appropriate first-line laxative 46% (n=7)

audits.intervention: Ward-based teaching, drop-in sessions and a six-point standardised checklist

cycle2.result: Abdominal exam 86%; medication review 80%; first-line laxative prescribing 80%

audits.other_findings: Baseline gaps included per rectal examination.
audits.citation: Yirdaw BG, Shaikh HA, Adekiya V. Improving the Assessment and Management of Constipation in Elderly Inpatients: A Quality Improvement Project in a Geriatric Ward. Cureus. 2026;18(9):e116396. doi:10.7759/cureus.116396. PMID: 42756715.
